items.stem: Explain the term “isotopes”.
items.answer: Atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

items.stem: Give the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in ²⁴Mg²⁺ (atomic number of Mg = 12).
items.markingKey: Protons = Z = 12; neutrons = A − Z = 24 − 12 = 12; electrons = Z − charge = 10.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The mass of a proton is about equal to the mass of an electron.
Reason (R): Very few α-particles were deflected by nearly 180°.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: A proton is about 1840 times heavier than an electron. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: An observation from an experiment is: the angular momentum of the electron is quantised; energy is emitted only when an electron jumps from a higher to a lower orbit; electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits of definite energy. Which atomic model or conclusion does it support? Give a reason.
items.answer: Bohr's model
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Bohr's model; 1 mark: the features the angular momentum of the electron is quantised; energy is emitted only when an electron jumps from a higher to a lower orbit; electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits of definite energy are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Cathode rays are deflected towards the positive plate in an electric field.
Reason (R): Cathode rays consist of negatively charged particles.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Negative particles are attracted by a positive plate.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A species has 9 protons, 10 neutrons and 10 electrons. Which species is it?
items.answer: ¹⁹F⁻
options: ¹⁹F⁻
²⁰Ne
²⁰F⁻
¹⁹F

items.stem: Which term describes the protons and neutrons present in the nucleus?
items.answer: nucleons
items.markingKey: (d) Nucleons: the protons and neutrons present in the nucleus.
options: canal rays
isotopes
isobars
nucleons

items.stem: Which of the following is a discovery or result of Rutherford?
items.answer: the α-particle scattering experiment with gold foil
items.markingKey: (a) The α-particle scattering experiment with gold foil is a discovery or result of Rutherford; the others are not.
options: the α-particle scattering experiment with gold foil
the neutron, by bombarding beryllium with α-particles
the plum pudding model of the atom
the charge-to-mass ratio of the electron

items.stem: Which of the following is a discovery of James Chadwick?
items.answer: the neutron, by bombarding beryllium with α-particles
items.markingKey: (b) The neutron, by bombarding beryllium with α-particles is a discovery of James Chadwick; the others are not.
options: the charge on the electron from the oil drop experiment
the neutron, by bombarding beryllium with α-particles
the nuclear model of the atom
the α-particle scattering experiment with gold foil

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Most α-particles were deflected through large angles by the gold foil.”
items.answer: Most α-particles passed through undeflected; only a few were deflected through large angles.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Most α-particles passed through undeflected; only a few were deflected through large angles.

items.stem:
An observation from an experiment is: the angular momentum of the electron is quantised; energy is emitted only when an electron jumps from a higher to a lower orbit.
(i) Which atomic model or conclusion does it support? (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were Thomson's plum pudding model? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Bohr's model (ii) electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits of definite energy (iii) the positive charge is spread uniformly through the atom; mass is assumed to be distributed uniformly
items.markingKey: (i) Bohr's model – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits of definite energy – 1 mark. (iii) for Thomson's plum pudding model: the positive charge is spread uniformly through the atom; electrons are embedded like seeds in a watermelon; mass is assumed to be distributed uniformly – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Explain the term “the work function”.
items.answer: The minimum energy needed to remove an electron from the surface of a metal.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the minimum energy needed to remove an electron from the surface of a metal.

items.stem: Light of wavelength 450 nm is emitted by an LED. Calculate its frequency and wavenumber. (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹)

Assertion (A): Electrons are ejected without any time lag when light of suitable frequency strikes the metal.
Reason (R): The energy of a photon is inversely proportional to its frequency.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: E = hν, so the energy of a photon is directly proportional to frequency.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Radio waves have a higher frequency than X-rays.”
items.answer: X-rays have a much higher frequency than radio waves.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: X-rays have a much higher frequency than radio waves.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The wave theory of light could not explain the photoelectric effect.
Reason (R): According to the wave theory, energy of light depends on its intensity.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) The wave theory predicts emission at any frequency for bright enough light, which is not observed.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
In an experiment on the photoelectric effect, the following data were obtained for a metal: light of 300 nm gives electrons with KE 1.84 eV; light of 400 nm gives electrons with KE 0.81 eV.
(i) Calculate the work function of the metal (hc = 1240 eV nm). (1 mark)
(ii) Find the threshold wavelength. (1 mark)
(iii) Would light of 600 nm eject electrons? Explain. (2 marks)
items.markingKey: (i) 1 mark (either data point gives ≈ 2.29 eV). (ii) 1 mark. (iii) 1 mark: E = 2.07 eV; 1 mark: less than W₀ so no emission.

items.stem: The work function of potassium is 2.25 eV. Calculate its threshold frequency and threshold wavelength. (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, 1 eV = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ J)
items.answer: ν₀ = 5.44 × 10¹⁴ s⁻¹; λ₀ = 551 nm

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct increasing order of photon energy: yellow light, violet light, green light, blue light. Give a reason.
items.answer: yellow light < green light < blue light < violet light
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order yellow light < green light < blue light < violet light; 1 mark for the reason: E = hc/λ; wavelength decreases from red (~700 nm) to violet (~400 nm), so photon energy increases.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct increasing order of wavelength?
items.answer: X-rays < visible light < infrared < microwaves
items.markingKey: (a) X-rays < visible light < infrared < microwaves. Wavelength increases (and frequency decreases) from X-rays to radio waves in the electromagnetic spectrum.
options: X-rays < visible light < infrared < microwaves
visible light < microwaves < X-rays < infrared
microwaves < X-rays < infrared < visible light
X-rays < microwaves < visible light < infrared

items.stem: Explain the term “a quantum”.
items.answer: The smallest quantity of energy that can be emitted or absorbed in the form of electromagnetic radiation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the smallest quantity of energy that can be emitted or absorbed in the form of electromagnetic radiation.

items.stem: The work function of caesium is 1.9 eV. Light of wavelength 220 nm falls on its surface. Calculate the kinetic energy of the ejected electrons in eV. (hc = 1240 eV nm, approximately)
Define the term “a line spectrum”.
items.answer: A spectrum consisting of discrete bright lines with dark spaces between them.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a spectrum consisting of discrete bright lines with dark spaces between them.

items.stem: Calculate the radius of the n = 1 Bohr orbit of the He⁺ ion. (r₁ for hydrogen = 52.9 pm)

Assertion (A): The energy gap between successive Bohr orbits increases with n.
Reason (R): The angular momentum of an electron in a Bohr orbit is an integral multiple of h/2π.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: The energy gap between successive orbits decreases as n increases. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: How much energy is needed to ionise a hydrogen atom whose electron is in the n = 1 orbit? (E₁ = −2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ J)
items.markingKey: Ionisation energy = 0 − Eₙ = 2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸/1 = 2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ J.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The spectrum of hydrogen consists of discrete lines.
Reason (R): The electron in a hydrogen atom can have only certain definite energies.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Transitions between fixed energy levels give fixed frequencies, hence lines.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Give two limitations of Bohr's model of the atom.
items.answer: It cannot explain the spectra of multi-electron atoms; it cannot explain splitting of lines in magnetic (Zeeman) or electric (Stark) fields; it ignores the dual nature of the electron and the uncertainty principle.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any two limitations.

items.stem: To which series does the line produced by the transition n = 6 → n = 4 in the hydrogen spectrum belong?
items.answer: Brackett
items.markingKey: (d) Lines ending at n = 4 form the Brackett series.
options: Paschen
Pfund
Lyman
Brackett

items.stem: An electron in a hydrogen atom falls from n = 5 to n = 3. Calculate the wavelength of the radiation emitted and name the spectral series. (R_H = 109 677 cm⁻¹)
items.answer: 1282.2 nm; Paschen series (infrared)
items.markingKey: ν̄ = R_H(1/3² − 1/5²) = 7799 cm⁻¹ (1); λ = 1/ν̄ = 1282.2 nm (1); final level n = 3 ⇒ Paschen series (1).

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The radius of the n-th Bohr orbit is proportional to n.”
items.answer: The radius of the n-th orbit is proportional to n².
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The radius of the n-th orbit is proportional to n².

items.answer: Brackett

items.answer: The quantum number that gives the spatial orientation of an orbital.

items.answer: 1s

1p
2s
1s

items.stem: How many radial nodes and angular nodes does a 3d orbital have?
items.answer: 0 radial, 2 angular

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Wave nature of a moving cricket ball cannot be detected.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) λ = h/mv is tiny for large m.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: The position of an electron is measured within an uncertainty of 1 × 10⁻¹¹ m. Calculate the minimum uncertainty in its velocity. (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg)
items.markingKey: Δx · mΔv ≥ h/4π ⇒ Δv = h/(4π m Δx) = 5.79 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: An orbital has 1 radial node and 0 angular nodes. Identify the orbital.
items.answer: 2s
items.markingKey: (b) Angular nodes = l = 0 ⇒ s; radial nodes = n − l − 1 = 1 ⇒ n = 2; so 2s.
options: 2p
2s
3s
1s

items.stem: Why are electrons in a hydrogen atom with the same n but different l of equal energy, while in a multi-electron atom they are not?
items.answer: In hydrogen the energy depends only on n. In multi-electron atoms, inner electrons shield the nucleus; s electrons penetrate closer to the nucleus than p, p more than d, so they feel a larger effective nuclear charge and have lower energy.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: energy depends only on n for H; 1 mark: shielding/penetration in multi-electron atoms.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct increasing order of number of radial nodes: 2p, 5p, 4p. Give a reason.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order 2p < 4p < 5p; 1 mark for the reason: Radial nodes = n − l − 1, so for p orbitals it is 0, 1, 2, 3.

items.stem: (a) Write the four quantum numbers for each electron in the 2p subshell of nitrogen, following Hund's rule. (b) How many orbitals are there for n = 4, and how many of them are d orbitals? (c) Explain why l = 3 is not possible for n = 3.
items.answer: (a) n = 2, l = 1, mₗ = −1, 0, +1 each with mₛ = +½. (b) 16 orbitals; 5 are 4d. (c) l can only take values 0 to n − 1 = 2.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 marks; (b) 2 marks; (c) 1 mark.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “In a multi-electron atom 4s is higher in energy than 3d.”
items.answer: In a multi-electron atom (e.g. K, Ca) 4s fills before 3d because it has a lower (n + l) value.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: In a multi-electron atom (e.g. K, Ca) 4s fills before 3d because it has a lower (n + l) value.

items.stem: What is the maximum number of electrons in the shell with n = 5?
items.markingKey: Number of orbitals = n² = 25; electrons = 2n² = 50.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A d subshell has five orbitals.
Reason (R): In a multi-electron atom 4s is higher in energy than 3d.

items.answer: A is true, but R is false.

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.answer: 2 radial, 1 angular

items.stem: The position of an electron is measured within an uncertainty of 5 × 10⁻¹¹ m. Calculate the minimum uncertainty in its velocity. (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg)
items.markingKey: Δx · mΔv ≥ h/4π ⇒ Δv = h/(4π m Δx) = 1.16 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: What is meant by “the Aufbau principle”?
items.answer: The principle that in the ground state orbitals are filled in order of increasing energy.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the principle that in the ground state orbitals are filled in order of increasing energy.

items.stem: Which is the ground-state electronic configuration of cobalt (Z = 27)?
items.answer: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 3d⁷

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “According to Hund's rule electrons pair up before they fill degenerate orbitals singly.”
items.answer: Electrons enter degenerate orbitals singly with parallel spins before pairing.

items.stem: Write the electronic configuration of phosphorus (Z = 15) and state the number of unpaired electrons in its ground state.
items.answer: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p³; 3 unpaired electrons
items.markingKey: Configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p³ (1); by Hund's rule electrons occupy degenerate orbitals singly first, giving 3 unpaired (1).

items.stem: Which of the following atoms has the largest number of unpaired electrons in its ground state? nickel (Z = 28), aluminium (Z = 13), calcium (Z = 20), scandium (Z = 21)
items.answer: nickel (Z = 28)

nickel (Z = 28)
calcium (Z = 20)

items.stem: Which term describes the principle that no two electrons in an atom can have the same set of four quantum numbers?
items.answer: Pauli's exclusion principle

the Aufbau principle
the (n + l) rule

An orbital can hold a maximum of two electrons with opposite spins.
In forming Fe²⁺, two 3d electrons are removed from iron.

items.answer: [Ar]; 0 unpaired

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The 4s orbital is filled before 3d.

items.stem: What is meant by “valence electrons”?
items.answer: The electrons in the outermost shell of an atom.

items.stem: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of a cricket ball of mass 0.1 kg moving with a velocity of 40 m s⁻¹. (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s)
items.markingKey: λ = h/mv = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ / (0.1 kg × 40) = 1.66 × 10⁻³⁴ m. Such a tiny wavelength cannot be detected, so wave nature is unimportant for macroscopic objects.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about electromagnetic radiation and quantum theory is correct?
items.answer: The kinetic energy of photoelectrons increases with the frequency of incident light.

items.stem: A 10 W lamp emits monochromatic light of wavelength 500 nm. How many photons does it emit in 10 s? (Assume all the power is emitted as light; h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹)

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The Lyman series of hydrogen lies in the visible region.”
items.answer: The Lyman series lies in the ultraviolet region; the Balmer series is visible.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The Lyman series lies in the ultraviolet region; the Balmer series is visible.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between Thomson's plum pudding model and Bohr's model on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An observation from an experiment is: electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits of definite energy. Which atomic model or conclusion does it support – Thomson's plum pudding model or Bohr's model? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Thomson's plum pudding model: the positive charge is spread uniformly through the atom; electrons are embedded like seeds in a watermelon; mass is assumed to be distributed uniformly. Bohr's model: electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits of definite energy; energy is emitted only when an electron jumps from a higher to a lower orbit; the angular momentum of the electron is quantised. (b) Bohr's model.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: Bohr's model; 1 mark: “electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits of definite energy” is a feature of Bohr's model.

items.stem: Which term describes the ejection of electrons from a metal surface when light of suitable frequency falls on it?
items.answer: the photoelectric effect
items.markingKey: (c) The photoelectric effect: the ejection of electrons from a metal surface when light of suitable frequency falls on it.
options: black body radiation
wavenumber
the photoelectric effect
the work function

items.stem:
Assertion (A): According to Hund's rule electrons pair up before they fill degenerate orbitals singly.
Reason (R): Copper has the configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Electrons enter degenerate orbitals singly with parallel spins before pairing. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The 3d orbital has two radial nodes.”
items.answer: A 3d orbital has n − l − 1 = 0 radial nodes and two angular nodes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: A 3d orbital has n − l − 1 = 0 radial nodes and two angular nodes.

items.stem: Write the electronic configuration of Cu⁺ (Z of Cu = 29) and give the number of unpaired electrons. Explain which electrons are removed first.
items.answer: [Ar] 3d¹⁰; 0 unpaired
items.markingKey: Electrons are removed first from 4s (outermost, higher n), then 3d: Cu⁺ = [Ar] 3d¹⁰ (1); unpaired = 0 (1).

items.stem: What is the energy of a photon of light of wavelength 700 nm? (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹)
Which of the following sets of quantum numbers is allowed for an electron?
items.markingKey: (b) n = 3, l = 2, mₗ = 0, mₛ = −½ is allowed: l ranges 0…n − 1, mₗ from −l to +l, mₛ = ±½. The others break one rule (l = n, |mₗ| > l, or mₛ = 0).

items.stem: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of a cricket ball of mass 0.16 kg moving with a velocity of 25 m s⁻¹. (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s)
items.markingKey: λ = h/mv = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ / (0.16 kg × 25) = 1.66 × 10⁻³⁴ m. Such a tiny wavelength cannot be detected, so wave nature is unimportant for macroscopic objects.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about electromagnetic radiation and quantum theory is correct?
items.answer: The number of photoelectrons ejected is proportional to the intensity of light.
items.markingKey: (c) The number of photoelectrons ejected is proportional to the intensity of light. The other statements are false. Intensity increases the number of photoelectrons; their kinetic energy depends on frequency. No electrons are ejected below the threshold frequency, however intense the light. X-rays have a much higher frequency than radio waves.
options: Red light of very high intensity can eject electrons from any metal.
Increasing the intensity of light increases the kinetic energy of photoelectrons.
The number of photoelectrons ejected is proportional to the intensity of light.
Radio waves have a higher frequency than X-rays.

items.stem: Which term describes a spectrum consisting of discrete bright lines with dark spaces between them?
items.answer: a line spectrum
items.markingKey: (d) A line spectrum: a spectrum consisting of discrete bright lines with dark spaces between them.
options: an absorption spectrum
the ground state
an emission spectrum
a line spectrum

items.answer: chromium (Z = 24)

items.stem: An observation from an experiment is: the angular momentum of the electron is quantised; electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits of definite energy. Which atomic model or conclusion does it support? Give a reason.
items.answer: Bohr's model
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Bohr's model; 1 mark: the features the angular momentum of the electron is quantised; electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits of definite energy are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about subatomic particles and early atomic models is correct?
items.answer: The neutron was discovered by Chadwick in 1932.
items.markingKey: (b) The neutron was discovered by Chadwick in 1932. The other statements are false. Most α-particles passed through undeflected; only a few were deflected through large angles. The e/m of canal-ray particles depends on the gas in the tube. In Thomson's model the positive charge is spread uniformly over a sphere with electrons embedded in it.
options: In Thomson's model the positive charge is concentrated in a small nucleus.
The neutron was discovered by Chadwick in 1932.
Canal rays have the same e/m value for all gases.
Most α-particles were deflected through large angles by the gold foil.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct increasing order of energy of orbitals in a multi-electron atom?
items.markingKey: (a) 3s < 4s < 3d < 5s. By the (n + l) rule: lower n + l has lower energy; for equal n + l, lower n is lower in energy.

items.stem: A 60 W lamp emits monochromatic light of wavelength 400 nm. How many photons does it emit in 10 s? (Assume all the power is emitted as light; h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹)
items.answer: 1.21 × 10²¹ photons
items.markingKey: Energy per photon = hc/λ = 4.97 × 10⁻¹⁹ J (1); energy emitted = 60 × 10 = 600 J (1); N = 600/4.97 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 1.21 × 10²¹ (1).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom is correct?
items.answer: The angular momentum of an electron in a Bohr orbit is an integral multiple of h/2π.
items.markingKey: (a) The angular momentum of an electron in a Bohr orbit is an integral multiple of h/2π. The other statements are false. The Lyman series lies in the ultraviolet region; the Balmer series is visible. It fails for multi-electron atoms and cannot explain fine structure or the Zeeman and Stark effects. The energy gap between successive orbits decreases as n increases.
options: The angular momentum of an electron in a Bohr orbit is an integral multiple of h/2π.
The Lyman series of hydrogen lies in the visible region.
The energy gap between successive Bohr orbits increases with n.
Bohr's theory explains the spectra of multi-electron atoms well.

Half-filled and completely filled subshells have extra stability.
Chromium has the configuration [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹.
Nitrogen has three unpaired electrons in its ground state.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between Thomson's plum pudding model and Rutherford's nuclear model on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An observation from an experiment is: electrons are embedded like seeds in a watermelon. Which atomic model or conclusion does it support – Thomson's plum pudding model or Rutherford's nuclear model? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Thomson's plum pudding model: the positive charge is spread uniformly through the atom; electrons are embedded like seeds in a watermelon; mass is assumed to be distributed uniformly. Rutherford's nuclear model: most of the space in the atom is empty; the positive charge and most of the mass are concentrated in a tiny nucleus; a few α-particles bounce back from a thin gold foil. (b) Thomson's plum pudding model.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: Thomson's plum pudding model; 1 mark: “electrons are embedded like seeds in a watermelon” is a feature of Thomson's plum pudding model.

items.stem: Calculate the energy of one mole of photons of radiation of wavelength 450 nm. (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, Nₐ = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
